metadata.methods_description: Individual intensities were first calibrated so that laser stimulation corresponded to average pain ratings of 4 and 7. Participants then received a fixed-intensity laser stimulus about every 20 seconds, in 4 blocks of 40 trials. They fixated on a cross with eyes open. After each stimulus there was a 3-second pause, followed by a 5-second window in which they rated pain intensity from 0 to 10. The next trial began 1-3 seconds after the rating.

citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises neuroimaging recordings from participants undergoing laser pain stimulation with concurrent pain rating assessments. This is a NEMAR-hosted reorganization of OpenNeuro dataset ds005285. Participants received 160 laser stimulations of varying intensities across 4 blocks, with pain ratings collected on a 0-10 scale. The study investigates pain perception and modulation mechanisms, with potential applications to understanding pain processing and therapeutic interventions.
